name: Last-mile delivery and proof of delivery
one_line: The final handover record for one parcel or consignment at its delivery point: an attempt or delivery event, recipient or safe-place outcome, timestamp, location evidence, signature or scan, package condition and any refusal, damage or exception. A doorstep image, address, tracking event, appointment or signature alone is not proof of this situation. Placeholder template: the logistics schema remains field-less pending R1c.

deterministic: a proof-of-delivery record whose labelled or structured slots join one consignment or parcel reference to delivered/attempted status, date/time, delivery point or geocoded event, recipient or safe-place outcome, and a receiver signature, scan, PIN or carrier event acknowledgement

a delivery-app event export whose rows join tracking or consignment identity to driver/route stop, event timestamp, GPS or delivery-zone evidence, recipient status, signature/PIN/photo indicator and exception code

a doorstep photo submission whose native message or form metadata binds the image to one delivery reference and event, while the image itself shows parcel, door/hand-off context or exception condition; camera EXIF alone never establishes delivery

a delivery exception structure joining parcel/consignment identity to attempted-delivery time, reason such as refused, inaccessible, damaged or safe-place, driver note, recipient communication and reattempt/return outcome

a recipient signature or electronic acceptance packet pairing shipment identity with signer/recipient role, delivered time/place, package count or condition and carrier system event; a signature image detached from these roles is not enough
a locker, collection-point or neighbour handover record joining parcel reference to compartment/pickup point, release timestamp, recipient code or scan and collection status
a last-mile damage or shortage report joining one parcel/consignment to package condition at delivery, photographs or inspection, recipient exception, carrier review and claim/return status

a carrier delivery-status feed that includes final-mile event semantics and package/consignment identity, not merely generic in-transit timestamps; the row-level status and attempt/delivery reason are required

an email or message whose native sender/recipient/subject and body or attachment bind a parcel reference to a completed delivery, failed attempt, safe-place instruction or recipient dispute, with a delivery event cited

an archive manifest exposing one parcel's label, route event, doorstep image, signature capture, exception note and claim/return records; the manifest is inspected without unpacking and does not propagate facts to members
a delivery receipt scan or OCR page whose own labels preserve parcel identity, recipient/attempt status, delivered time/place and acknowledgement, even when handwriting or print is partly degraded
needs_llm: whether an image shows a completed doorstep delivery, an attempted delivery, a staged parcel, a warehouse pallet or an unrelated product photograph when no reference is legible
whether a delivery address is a final destination, depot, safe place, sender address, carrier office or camera capture location when role labels are incomplete
whether a signature, PIN or scan indicates recipient acceptance, driver completion, a locker release or only an internal status update
whether a damage/shortage note was recorded at final delivery, during warehouse receipt, in transit or after opening, and whether it is allegation or verified condition
whether a carrier status export's last event represents actual delivery, a failed attempt, neighbour/safe-place handover, collection-point arrival or return-to-sender
whether a parcel label or QR code in a photograph binds to the same consignment as a nearby POD record; barcode visibility alone cannot establish ownership or event
whether an email thread or customer message is a delivery confirmation, a planned appointment, a complaint, a returns request or an automated marketing notice
whether a mixed archive contains one parcel event or many unrelated stops and recipients; member facts must not be copied across the archive
whether OCR-poor handwritten proof preserves enough event and recipient-role structure to activate, with unknown returned when evidence cannot be cited
whether a calendar collection/delivery appointment became a completed handover without a separate scan, signature, photo or carrier event
multilingual last-mile forms, safe-place instructions and exception descriptions outside the local delivery vocabulary
never_alone: the words delivered, delivery, doorstep, proof of delivery, POD, attempted, refused, safe place, parcel, courier, recipient or signature alone
a parcel, tracking, consignment, order, route, locker, PIN, barcode, QR code or delivery-reference token outside a labelled role and event structure
an address, door number, GPS coordinate, map, timestamp or geotag alone; each can describe a plan, depot, sender, receiver, route or camera capture
a parcel, pallet, doorstep, signature, driver, uniform, vehicle or delivery-app screenshot alone
a carrier, courier, marketplace, retailer, buyer, seller or recipient name alone
a delivered/failed status, scan, PIN, photo, signature, safe-place note or exception word alone
a purchase order, invoice, order confirmation, shipping label, carrier tracking page or returns label alone
a source_type or extension alone, including PDF, spreadsheet, image, OCR, email, calendar, archive or opaque binary
a parent folder named Deliveries, POD, Parcels, Shipping, Courier, Orders or Returns alone
membership in one download, upload, email thread, portal session or archive alone; 00 states: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic"
missing EXIF as proof that an image is a screenshot, or present GPS as proof that a photograph was taken at the delivery point
a carrier event timestamp without a package/consignment identity and final-mile attempt or handover semantics

work_types: delivery dispute and carrier claim packet
grouping_reasons: one parcel/consignment across label, route stop, attempt, doorstep image, signature/PIN, recipient message and final status
one failed delivery across attempt event, reason, safe-place or collection instruction, reattempt and return-to-sender evidence
one damage or shortage exception across delivery photo, receiver note, carrier review, claim, replacement and return records
one locker, neighbour or safe-place handover across release code, scan, recipient confirmation and dispute evidence
one delivery route's final-mile events when each member retains its own parcel identity and no stop's recipient fact is copied to another
a sparse doorstep photo, email or calendar entry may join an accepted delivery group without receiving parcel, recipient, address or delivery facts; grouping does not copy labels

template.why: The logistics schema declares no legal fields under PR-6, so this template does not write consignment, carrier, asset, site or record_type dimensions. Conditional on R1c promoting those proposals, the useful projection is consignment/parcel -> delivery event or record_type, with route or depot only where those are genuinely the file's subject. Recipient names, delivery addresses, coordinates, safe-place details and driver identities are evidence and privacy-sensitive values, not default folder dimensions. This differs from logistics.shipment's full custody dossier because last-mile POD is a final-handover situation with recipient/attempt semantics, event proof and delivery exceptions; it should not require the upstream bill-of-lading, customs or origin chain. It is not time-first: 00 says, "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." No executable dimension is claimed until R1c licenses a canonical key.

observations: image shows a parcel at a doorway with a carrier-app overlay and partly legible consignment reference
camera EXIF and capture time are present
recipient, delivery status and exact address are not fully legible
must_not_conclude: delivery or recipient acceptance from the image alone
that the parcel belongs to the nearby CMR

observations: payload fields identify parcel/consignment, route stop, event time, delivery status and recipient/driver scan state
location evidence and exception code are separate fields
no raw image is embedded in the payload
must_not_conclude: recipient identity beyond the labelled role
that a GPS point is a home address
physical package condition without a cited image or note

observations: form joins consignment reference to delivered-at time/place, recipient role, package count and signature block
delivery status and damage/shortage boxes are labelled
carrier acknowledgement and receiver acknowledgement are distinct
must_not_conclude: that recipient is owner of the goods
absence of a damage tick as proof of perfect condition

observations: native sender/recipient/subject identify an attempted delivery and consignment reference
body contains failed-attempt reason, reattempt window and collection-point instruction
no completed delivery event is attached
must_not_conclude: recipient identity from the sender address alone

observations: rows join parcel reference to locker/collection point, release scan, code status, pickup time and collection state
recipient notification state is separate from collection confirmation
no origin shipment or carrier contract fields are present
must_not_conclude: recipient identity from a locker code alone
that a parcel was not damaged before locker placement

observations: receiver/driver roles and consignment reference are labelled
package condition, seal, shortage and photograph references are recorded at final handover
claim review and settlement status are separate from the allegation
must_not_conclude: that the receiver's account is correct without review

observations: PDF has no usable text layer and OCR recovers partial parcel reference, recipient/attempt status, date and signature labels
handwritten safe-place note is visible but incomplete
scanner metadata names a device rather than a carrier or recipient
must_not_conclude: recipient, address or delivery status where OCR is unreadable

observations: rows contain package reference, stop sequence, attempt/delivery/return event, timestamps and exception codes
some rows have driver and geofence fields
the export contains many parcels and no single delivery subject
must_not_conclude: one recipient or address for the whole export
delivery completion from an event label without package context

observations: manifest lists label, route event, doorstep image, signature capture, failed-attempt notice and damage claim
archive has not been unpacked
one member name references a different parcel and requires member-level review
must_not_conclude: one recipient, address or status for every member
that all listed members are final-mile evidence

observations: event names a planned delivery window and address
organizer, attendee and start/end fields are present
no completed scan, signature, photo or exception event is attached
must_not_conclude: address role from the calendar event alone

observations: return label identifies parcel reference, carrier, origin/destination and barcode
reason-for-return or recipient acceptance is absent
label is prepared for movement but does not prove a failed final-mile attempt
must_not_conclude: delivery failure from a return label alone

observations: camera photo shows a pallet and carrier label in a warehouse
no final recipient, doorstep, handover or delivery-event evidence is visible
EXIF capture time is present
must_not_conclude: last-mile delivery from a label or pallet image
that the pallet was delivered rather than received/held

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Recipient-Signature_CN-4021.pdf. logistics.last-mile-pod wins when final-handover event, recipient/attempt status and delivery proof are central; logistics.shipment wins when the same bytes are one member of a full consignment custody dossier spanning origin, carrier, customs, packages and destination, and a signed page alone cannot establish the upstream movement.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Delivery-Appointment_CN-4021.ics. last-mile-pod wins when the same bytes are tied to a completed delivery attempt or handover evidence; logistics.route-dispatch wins when they are a working-day plan of driver, vehicle, ordered stops and planned-versus-actual route performance, and an appointment alone proves neither execution nor receipt.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Driver-App-Completed_CN-4021.json. last-mile-pod wins when the same bytes document a parcel's final-mile event and recipient/exception outcome; logistics.fleet-vehicle wins when they are vehicle, driver, licensing, telematics or operator-compliance records, and a driver or vehicle identifier does not itself prove a delivery.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Parcel-Return-Label_CN-4021.pdf. last-mile-pod wins when the same bytes are linked to a failed delivery, recipient refusal or carrier return event; retail_hospitality.returns-warranty wins when return authorization, customer refund/replacement and product-return disposition are central, and a return label alone proves neither.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Failed-Attempt_CN-4021.eml. last-mile-pod wins when delivery attempt, parcel reference and final-mile event are evidenced; business_operations.customer-account-management wins when the same bytes are a customer complaint/service interaction and the shipment event is incidental, and a recipient message alone cannot establish either workflow.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Damage-at-Door_CN-4021.pdf. last-mile-pod wins when final delivery condition, recipient exception and carrier handover are central; manufacturing.production-record wins when the same bytes are an incoming product/lot inspection or quarantine disposition, and a package condition note does not decide whether damage occurred in transit or manufacturing.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Scanned-POD_CN-4021.pdf. last-mile-pod wins when OCR recovers parcel, final-mile event and acknowledgement structure; photos.scanned-documents wins when the same bytes are retained as a scanned image/document without a delivery-event relation, and OCR text or a signature-like mark alone is insufficient.

sensitivity_why: Recipient names, home or workplace addresses, geolocation, delivery schedules, driver and vehicle identifiers, package contents, safe-place instructions, signatures, PINs, photographs and claims can expose personal routines, access information or commercial movements. This row assigns no handling class; P7's file-level classification and local/cloud policy remain authoritative.
open_question: NJ-LOG-POD-1: R1c must decide whether this template reuses logistics proposals `consignment`, `carrier`, `asset`, `site` and `record_type`, and whether a final-mile event needs a neutral global key. NJ-LOG-POD-2: Should a signed or photographed POD be mutex with logistics.shipment, or may the same bytes activate both the complete consignment and final-mile templates when their evidence roles are independently present? NJ-LOG-POD-3: Delivery images, return labels and failed-attempt emails may also support Photos, Retail/Hospitality, Business Operations and Manufacturing; should P9 represent coactivation, or must a user choose custody/purpose? This template deliberately authors no also_holds_with edge. NJ-LOG-POD-4: R2/R4 must settle deployment-specific parcel, consignment, geofence, locker and carrier event validation; no regex, address inference, recipient identity or legal delivery threshold is asserted here.
